hyperedges.label: Encrypted Provider and Model Selection Flow

nodes.label: _pi_provider_menu()
nodes.rationale: Now carries two explicit shell-indexing invariants written into the code as comments: (1) non-numeric input is rejected before any arithmetic comparison, because zsh arithmetic evaluation of a non-numeric string can expand/execute it; (2) `providers[$choice]` is indexed with the raw menu number because zsh arrays are 1-indexed, so the bash-style `choice-1` offset is deliberately NOT applied.

nodes.label: _pi_model_menu()
nodes.rationale: Indexes model_ids with the raw menu number; the in-code comment records that subtracting 1 (bash habit) selected the previous model in the list and selected nothing at all for choice 1. Parses the INI-style .pi_models.conf with an inline awk section matcher rather than sourcing it, so the config file never executes.

nodes.label: _pi_handle_providers()
nodes.rationale: Orchestrates the two documented workflows (first-time init vs standard execution) and self-heals a missing .pi_models.conf by writing a default via here-document. Credentials are injected as an exported {PROVIDER}_API_KEY environment variable rather than a CLI flag, because the `pi` binary reads the key from the environment; only --provider/--model go on the command line.

nodes.label: _pi_parse_args()
nodes.rationale: Loop is now 1..argc inclusive. The in-code comment records the bug it replaces: iterating 0..n-1 read the empty slot 0 and never reached the final element, which prepended an empty argument and silently dropped the last one (e.g. the value of --model). Mutates the caller's pi_args array in place through dynamic scoping.

nodes.label: _pi_handle_resume()
nodes.rationale: The listed session number from `cat -n` is used directly as the zsh array index into session_files, since both are 1-based. Session list ordering comes from `ls -1t` (mtime), which is what makes append-on-resume keep a continued session at the top.

nodes.label: _pi_run_new_session()
nodes.rationale: Records to a PID-suffixed temp file and installs an EXIT trap that renames the partial log to *_INCOMPLETE.log, so an abrupt Ctrl+C never loses transcript data. The trap is cleared with `trap - EXIT` immediately after `script` returns so the normal naming path runs instead.

nodes.label: Zsh Environment Bootstrap
nodes.rationale: nilesh.sh is the single entry point sourced by the user's shell: it sets PATH/tool homes, then sources .service_manager and .pi_customization so that app.* and pi() become available as interactive shell functions. Keeping the app launcher and the pi wrapper in separate sourced files (rather than inline) is what lets each be edited/reloaded independently via `source.env.script`.

nodes.label: Zsh 1-Indexed Array Invariant
nodes.rationale: zsh arrays start at index 1, unlike bash arrays which start at 0. The file now encodes this as an explicit, commented invariant in every place a user-visible menu number is turned into an array subscript: the printed number IS the subscript, and no `-1` offset is applied. Violating it produced two distinct symptom classes - off-by-one selection (picking the previous entry, and nothing for choice 1) in the provider/model/session menus, and, in argument parsing, an empty leading element plus a silently dropped final element. A companion invariant guards non-numeric menu input before it reaches zsh arithmetic evaluation.

nodes.label: In-Memory-Only Credential Handling
nodes.rationale: Provider keys live on disk only inside .pi_providers.enc (openssl aes-256-cbc + pbkdf2, chmod 600). The password and decrypted plaintext exist only in shell locals for the life of the pi() call; decryption stderr is discarded and openssl's non-zero exit is the sole bad-password signal. Nothing decrypted is ever written back to disk.

nodes.label: Per-Provider Model Catalog
nodes.rationale: INI-style catalog mapping model_id to a friendly display name, sectioned per provider. Externalising the catalog means new models are added by editing config, not the shell function. The live file has drifted from the default here-document baked into _pi_handle_providers: it adds gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-astra (whose display names smuggle in per-million-token pricing, since the menu shows only the friendly name).

nodes.label: APP_MAP
nodes.rationale: Single associative-array declaration of every managed app as name -> "dir:invocation[:ports]", so directories need no common parent and adding an app is a one-line change. The optional ports field exists because wrappers like `npm run dev` / `npx vite` fork a child that actually binds the port and that child can be orphaned to PID 1, severing parent/child tracking.

nodes.label: _app.csv
nodes.rationale: Exists purely to guard a zsh splitting gotcha: splitting an empty string with (@s:,:) yields one empty element instead of zero, so every caller would otherwise iterate once over an empty port.

nodes.label: _app.is_running
nodes.rationale: Liveness is judged by a listening port when the app declares one, because that is ground truth regardless of how the process tree forked; the recorded launcher PID is only the fallback for portless apps. The $2 override exists for app.start, which knows the freshly-resolved ports before any portfile for that run exists.

nodes.label: _app.resolve
nodes.rationale: Accepts either an APP_MAP key or an ad-hoc "dir:command[:ports]" spec, and returns a pipe-joined "name|dir|cmd|ports" record that callers split with IFS read. The trailing field is treated as ports only if it matches ^[0-9]+(,[0-9]+)*$, so commands that themselves contain a colon are not mis-parsed.

nodes.label: app.start
nodes.rationale: Launches via nohup in a subshell, records pid/pgid/ports sidecar files under $APP_RUN_DIR, then polls lsof up to 20 times at 0.3s for the declared ports so 'started' means 'actually listening' rather than 'launcher forked'.

nodes.label: app.stop
nodes.rationale: Kills the union of the recorded launcher PID, every PID in its process group, and whatever currently owns the configured ports - deduplicated through an associative `seen` array - because npm/npx children get detached or reparented to PID 1 and would otherwise survive. TERM first, then re-checks (including ports) and KILLs survivors; stale sidecar files are cleaned up when nothing is running.

nodes.label: Sidecar PID/PGID/Port State Files
nodes.rationale: Per-app state is kept as flat files ($name.pid, $name.pgid, $name.ports, $name.log) under $APP_RUN_DIR (default ~/.local/state/app-launcher) so that status and stop work from any new shell, not just the one that started the app. Three separate tracking handles are stored because no single one survives every forking/orphaning pattern.

nodes.label: Robust Recording and Naming (spec 1.1)
nodes.rationale: Logs are named at session END, not start, so the timestamp reflects when work finished; a trap preserves an _INCOMPLETE log on abrupt termination rather than losing the transcript; naming is a prioritized chain (--name flag > post-session prompt > timestamp fallback) so the common case needs no decision up front.

nodes.label: True Session Continuation (spec 1.2)
nodes.rationale: Resume appends to the ORIGINAL log with `script -a` instead of creating a new file, which both keeps one continuous transcript and bumps the file's mtime - and since the resume listing is sorted by most-recently-modified, a continued session correctly floats to the top next time.

nodes.label: Helper-Function Refactoring (spec 2)
nodes.rationale: The monolithic pi() is decomposed into single-responsibility helpers with pi() reduced to an orchestrator, for readability and maintainability. The spec enumerates exactly five helpers; the implementation grew a second family (_pi_get_password, _pi_encrypt_providers, _pi_decrypt_providers, _pi_add_new_provider, _pi_provider_menu, _pi_model_menu, _pi_handle_providers) that the spec's list never updated.

nodes.label: Encrypted Provider Storage (spec 3.1)
nodes.rationale: Per-project .pi_providers.enc encrypted with openssl aes-256-cbc, unlocked by a password prompted once per session; password and decrypted keys are held in memory only and never written to disk, so a stolen repo copy yields nothing usable.

nodes.label: Provider User Workflows (spec 3.2)
nodes.rationale: Two branches: first-time initialization (offer to create the file, set+confirm password, add first provider) and standard execution (prompt password, then a numbered menu of saved providers plus [Add a new provider] and [Continue without a provider]). Implemented in _pi_handle_providers/_pi_provider_menu, except that after adding a provider the implementation returns 1 and asks the user to re-run instead of continuing into selection.

nodes.label: Credential Injection (spec 3.2)
nodes.rationale: DIVERGENCE: the spec says the script injects `--provider` and `--api-key` arguments into the pi command line. The implementation injects `--provider` and `--model` and exports the key as {PROVIDER}_API_KEY instead, with an in-code comment explaining that `pi` expects the key as an environment variable, not a flag. The env-var route is also the safer one (the key never appears in the process argv / shell history), so the implementation is correct and the spec is stale. The spec likewise never mentions dynamic model selection or .pi_models.conf at all.

nodes.label: Filename Sanitization (spec 1.1)
nodes.rationale: All user-supplied session names are sanitized to valid filenames, since the name is taken from free-form interactive input and is used directly as a path component.
